title: Meet Falvorn AI. Intelligence without limits.
excerpt: A new home for our work in agent systems, private AI, and applied intelligence.
author: Falvorn AI
body: Falvorn AI brings a growing family of independent software projects into one place. Our focus is practical: make intelligent systems understandable, useful, and easier to explore.
Explore goal-driven browser tooling with Falvorn Agent, coordinated specialists with NEXUS-100, digital employees with AgentVerse, and evidence-aware retrieval with AutoRAG Router.

This website also introduces our private AI workbenches and applied intelligence projects. Each product carries its current development status. Public demos, desktop previews, and research are different stages of work, and we label them accordingly.
We welcome conversations about evaluations, collaborations, and product development. Use the contact section to get in touch.

title: Better answers start with better context.
excerpt: Why task-aware retrieval matters—and how to explore it in the AutoRAG lab.
author: Falvorn AI
body: A dependency question and a financial-record lookup need different kinds of context. Treating every request as the same search problem can hide useful structure.

AutoRAG Router makes that choice visible. Its public lab applies browser-side routing rules to a small sample knowledge base, selects a strategy, and shows matching evidence. The Python implementation provides a separate API baseline.

The current work includes hybrid lexical retrieval, explicit entity-tag graph lookups, structured filtering and bounded query decomposition. These are inspectable baseline techniques, not claims of native vision understanding or autonomous model reasoning.
Try different questions in the public routing lab. Inspect the evidence rather than treating a retrieval score as proof that an answer is correct.

title: A model is more than its weights.
excerpt: Planning private inference means accounting for context, runtime reserves, and headroom.
author: Falvorn AI
body: Parameter count is a useful starting point for planning, but it is only one part of an inference memory budget. Quantization overhead, KV cache, context length, concurrency, runtime allocations and operating-system reserves all matter.
SparkTwin exists to make those assumptions explicit. It lets engineers compare analytical configurations before spending time on a real deployment.

The memory playground on this website isolates just the weight-size calculation. It is intentionally simple: parameters multiplied by bits per weight, converted into GiB. It does not predict throughput or total deployment memory.
Use analytical estimates to choose what to measure next. Confirm actual consumption and performance with representative hardware, the chosen runtime, and real workloads.
